correctness.rationale: For the stated strip and a<1 the angular increment for F(z)=S(z) is exactly 1/2, forcing I=±ρ; each prime two-cycle has exactly one +ρ representative. Then b g(θ)=(2−γ)ρ and g=4 sin(2πθ) cos²(2πθ). On the positive half of the circle each interior root t=sin(2πθ) of 4t(1−t²)=(2−γ)ρ/b gives a reflected pair. This cubic peaks nondegenerately at t=1/√3, with nonzero angular second derivative and nonzero forcing derivative, proving both symmetry-class folds and the orbit counts. Independently, the derivative T of S∘F at a representative has trace γ−k and determinant −q, where k=2abρg′(θ). Since (S∘F)²=F² the return has trace (γ−k)²+2q and determinant q². Thus it is exponentially attracting exactly for 0<k<2γ, a saddle outside the closed interval, and has multipliers 1,q² at either endpoint. The reflected phase choices give opposite signs of k. On the positive branches k=2π(2a−1)(2−γ)|1−3s|/√(s(1−s)), s=t². Differentiating the square gives the sign of 3s−1, so each branch reaches 2γ exactly once; the two roots of the resulting quadratic give the stated thresholds. At the same b>b₀ the cubic roots x<y obey x²+xy+y²=1. For r=y/x>1, the square of the ratio of their positive k values is r(r+2)²/(2r+1)², which exceeds 1 because the numerator minus the denominator is r³−1. The low-t branch therefore crosses first, with the table including the boundary counts. A separate direct return-map differentiation and bisection at three parameter pairs corroborated the crossing values (replay: python /workspace/branches/review05_direct_return.py); the symbolic argument covers the entire range. The unit multipliers exclude exponential attraction at the boundaries, not all possible nonlinear attraction.

value.rationale: The symmetry picks out a natural class of periodic attractors of the studied map. A simultaneous birth does not imply a simultaneous later loss: the strict analytical separation gives a genuine one-sink regime for every admitted a and γ, even where a numerical period diagram would barely resolve the two crossings. The formulas and exact census are useful independently of global basin or bifurcation classification.
